cards.relevant: 美联储加息将影响全球金融市场、美元汇率及借贷成本，是重大经济政策转向信号。
cards.context: 美国通胀持续处于高位，美联储认为需要通过加息来抑制物价上涨。但特朗普希望低利率来维持经济增速，双方立场尖锐对立。
cards.source_analysis: BBC报道，立场中立，侧重事实陈述与政策影响分析。
cards.social_impact: 加息将推高房贷、信用卡和企业贷款成本，影响美国消费者和全球资本流动。
cards.source_text: US interest rates raised for first time in three years - Published US interest rates have been raised for the first time in more than three years and could be increased further in a bid to slow rising prices. Rates were hiked to 3.75%-4% from 3.5%-3.75% by the Federal Reserve in a unanimous decision, despite fierce opposition from President Donald Trump, who had called for rates to be cut. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the move was because "inflation is too high and has been for too long", adding that it was a "sober" and "responsible decision". However, Trump said rates "should be 1%, or less, because we are the Best Credit in the World - BY FAR". Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive for people wanting to secure loans, mortgages, and credit cards, but can lead to better returns on savings. Warsh said during a press conference on Wednesday following the decision that, while there was "an attitude of optimism" within the Fed leadership, inflation remained a problem. Like many central banks, the Fed has a target of keeping inflation at 2% or below. Warsh noted that US inflation has been above the target "for more than five years". That has helped make affordability one of the top concerns of American voters, who have seen fuel prices surge in response to soaring wholesale oil prices since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran. This has driven up the cost of many goods and services, as well. While the Fed "cannot affect any individual price – whether it be oil prices, whether it be food stuffs at the grocery store", Warsh said, the central bank can work to keep price rises from broadening across the economy. He added that strength in the jobs market and wider economy meant the Fed was staying focused on stabilising prices, and that those least well off had the most to gain from lower inflation. Central banks tend to increase rates when inflation is high to discourage spending and encourage saving, in the hope this will reduce the pace of price rises. But it's a balancing act, as higher rates can also encourage businesses to hold off on investing and hurt economic growth. What the higher rate means for Americans When he was confirmed, Democratic lawmakers had said Warsh would be Trump's "sock puppet" and many Fed watchers expected him to carry out Trump's persistent demands to slash rates. cards.relevant: 美俄关系持续紧张，新制裁可能进一步影响全球能源市场和地缘政治格局。

cards.social_impact: 新制裁可能影响俄罗斯经济及与美有业务往来的第三国企业。
cards.source_text: WASHINGTON, September 17. /TASS/. The House of Representatives of the US Congress has passed the bill to toughen anti-Russian sanctions previously approved by the Senate. During the vote, aired by the C-SPAN television channel, 262 members of the Republican-controlled House of Representatives voted in favor, while 159 were against. The bill, authored by the late Senator Lindsey Graham (designated as a terrorist and extremist in Russia), was passed by Congress on August 7. Once approved by the House, it will be submitted to President Donald Trump for signing. The document provides for restrictions on top Russian politicians and military officials, as well as state companies, along with secondary sanctions on Russia’s trading partners. The bill allows the US to impose 100% tariffs on the countries that are major buyers of Russian oil and gas, and also tighten sanctions on Iran.
cards.source_title: US Congress passes bill to toughen sanctions against Russia

cards.source_text: Photos show widespread damage at US sites from Iranian attacks - Published Images showing widespread damage to multiple US sites in the Middle East from Iranian strikes have been obtained by the BBC's US partner CBS. The photos, provided by active military personnel, show a severed radar jet, flattened trailers and severely damaged buildings. The undated photos were taken at US bases and sites in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. One member of the military, who was not named by CBS, said: "This is major damage to our bases that hasn't been communicated to the American public. "We're standing there with our eyes closed getting punched in the face." The White House referred the BBC to US Central Command. Centcom did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The photos, which have not been independently verified by the BBC, were published the day after a report from the Pentagon's watchdog confirmed hundreds of buildings and structures at US bases in the Middle East have been damaged and destroyed by Iran. One of the photos showed a destroyed Boeing E-3 Sentry at Prince Sultan Air Force Base in Saudi Arabia that has been ripped in half, its tail section crumpled into a tangled mess of metal. While the photo is undated, BBC Verify previously confirmed a similar photo, apparently of the same radar aircraft in March. The Boeing E-3 Awacs are used to detect and track potential targets at long ranges to provide an early warning of possible threats. At the time, a US official told Reuters that 12 US personnel had been wounded, two of them seriously, in an Iranian attack on the air base. A pair of undated images reportedly from Camp Beuhring, Kuwait, show crumpled trailers, and a large tent-like structure that had been reduced to shreds as smoke billowed from the site. Another image shows a four-storey building damaged by an Iranian strike at Camp Arifjan, in Kuwait. Damage to the site was reported in March, including on satellite communications hardware, though it is not clear whether this image is from the same attack. Brian Katulis, a former national security official under both Democratic and Republican administrations, said that the damage visible in the images showed that "America had not adequately prepared its defences". "And there is strong evidence that US adversaries like China and Russia may have helped Iran in targeting," added Katulis, now a senior fellow at the Middle East Institute. cards.source_text: Eight children among 21 killed after war-damaged Gaza building collapses, rescuers say - Published At least 21 people have been killed, including eight children, after a war-damaged building collapsed in the Gaza Strip overnight, rescuers and medics say. Witnesses told the BBC that the six-storey building in Gaza City's Tal al-Hawa area had been left tilting dangerously to one side after an Israeli strike more than a year ago. Displaced families had lived inside because they were desperate, they said. UN and Egyptian teams joined the search for survivors, which was slow due to a lack of equipment. Initially, rescuers from the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency had to use their bare hands. On Wednesday afternoon, they said they had ended the operation after taking 45 injured people to hospitals. Sherif, whose sister was killed, said: "They couldn't find a tent or somewhere to live. "This was the last place they could turn to, despite the danger. They were aware that it would likely end in tragedy. A lack of resources drove them towards certain death." A woman living in a tent nearby, Umm Mohammed Bakrun, said she had been talking to her son when the building collapsed suddenly in the early hours of Wednesday. "It felt like an earthquake. There was a loud sound and I couldn't stand up. Stones rained down on us and when I looked outside I saw a lot of dust," she told the BBC. "Within minutes, there were screams everywhere." Another witness, Mansour Abu Mohammed, said the building collapsed "in a few seconds". "Every day, a stone or a few stones would fall from it, but the people inside couldn't find anywhere else to live. I used to live next door to it and you could see that it was tilting to one side." Satellite imagery shows that the area around the building was targeted in the early weeks of the war, while damage to the building itself first became evident in 2024. The head of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Gaza office, Alessandro Mrakic, told reporters at the scene on Wednesday morning that "the situation... is tragic because we don't have the equipment and machinery that is needed". He also warned that approximately 400 other war-damaged buildings across Gaza were at imminent risk of collapse, particularly as winter approaches. "We need support, most importantly with machinery, equipment, among others. cards.title: 萨赫勒地区伊斯兰极端暴力今年将创历史新高

entities.name: 萨赫勒地区
entities.explain: 非洲撒哈拉沙漠以南的一条狭长地带，横跨马里、布基纳法索、尼日尔等国，近年来成为伊斯兰极端组织活跃的核心区域

entities.name: 基地组织
entities.explain: 全球知名的伊斯兰极端主义组织，2001年策划了震惊世界的9·11恐怖袭击

cards.summary: 据冲突监测机构ACLED统计，与基地组织和伊斯兰国有关联的武装团体在非洲萨赫勒地区发动了一系列大规模攻势，今年该地区的伊斯兰极端暴力事件预计将创下历史新高。这一数据发布正值美国纪念9·11袭击25周年之际，凸显基地组织在非洲持续扩张，与它在其他地区的相对衰弱形成鲜明对比。
cards.relevant: 9·11事件25年后，基地组织并未消亡，而是将重心转移至非洲萨赫勒地区，该地区正成为全球伊斯兰极端暴力的新中心，对国际安全格局有重大影响。
cards.context: 9·11事件后，美国主导的反恐战争削弱了基地组织在中东和阿富汗的力量，但该组织在非洲萨赫勒地区找到了新的立足点。近年来该地区政局动荡、政府控制力薄弱，为极端组织提供了扩张空间。
cards.source_analysis: 《卫报》是英国左倾主流媒体，长期关注非洲冲突和人权议题，报道倾向于强调西方反恐政策的局限性和地区人道危机。
cards.social_impact: 萨赫勒地区暴力事件持续攀升，影响范围覆盖马里、布基纳法索、尼日尔等多国，当地平民面临严重的安全威胁和大规模流离失所。
cards.source_text: Islamist extremist violence in Africa’s Sahel region is set to reach historic highs after a series of sweeping offensives by groups linked to al-Qaida and Islamic State, according to new figures compiled by the conflict monitor Acled. As the US marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks launched by al-Qaida against targets in Washington and New York, the statistics underline the continued expansion of the veteran organisation in parts of Africa – in stark contrast with its relative weakness elsewhere. Compiled by Acled, which stands for Armed Conflict Location and Event Data, the statistics focus on the centre of Islamic militancy in three countries – Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger – which together comprise a huge and hotly contested zone at the heart of the strategic Sahel region. According to the respected non-profit organisation, incidents of violence with jihadist groups present in the three countries have soared from 63 in 2016 to 2,845 in 2025. So far this year, 2,145 events have already been logged. If current trends continue in coming months, an annual total of well over 3,000 events appears likely. Though total deaths from terrorism globally have fallen to their lowest level since 2008, those in the Sahel have risen sharply. “Terrorism has become more geographically concentrated: the Sahel continued to record some of the world’s highest terrorism death tolls, with the UN recording more than 9,000 deaths from security incidents across Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger in 2025,” the 2026 report of the Global Peace Index noted earlier this year. In April, a joint offensive in Mali launched by the al-Qaida-linked group Jama’at Nusrat ul-Islam wa al-Muslimin (JNIM) and the Tuareg-dominated rebel group Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) targeted strategic towns, government forces and their Russian auxiliaries with ambushes, car bombs, drones and raids, inflicting significant casualties. Mali’s defence minister died in a suicide attack on his residence in the garrison town of Kati, 9 miles north-west of the capital, Bamako, and the head of military intelligence was killed. Other attacks hit Mali’s international airport, while rebels seized control of the strategic city of Kidal, a former stronghold of the FLA, after soldiers fled and a force of Russian mercenaries surrendered. cards.source_text: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member' - Published The president of the European Commission has backed proposals for Canada to become the EU's first "associate member". Ursula von der Leyen told the European Parliament on Wednesday she wanted to work on "opening the door" for Canada, which would involve closer ties on various key sectors. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney last week spoke of seeking a "unique alliance" with the EU. The country currently faces tense relations with the US, compounded by an intensifying dispute over trade. Without mentioning US President Donald Trump by name, von der Leyen said offering Canada some sort of EU membership was "not a partnership against anyone else, but for our common strength". She added: "Partnerships are a strategic choice for Europe. But they also respond to the fracture in the international rules-based system". Carney was in attendance at the annual key note speech in Strasbourg, and is due to address the parliament on Thursday. Trade talks between Canada and the US collapsed last month, sparking a series of new tariff measures. Trump's repeated talk of making Canada a "51st state" has also helped to fuel the feud between the North American neighbours. - Carney's new love-in with EU has everything to do with Trump - Published12 hours ago Von der Leyen told the EU's State of the Union address that the bloc and Canada "see the world with the same eyes", including on topics ranging from AI, to climate change and geopolitics. "And we have stood together: on Ukraine, on defence, on raw materials and on supply chains. But above all... Europe and Canada believe in democracy." She did not give specific details on how any Canadian membership would work, but listed manufacturing, technology, AI, defence, energy, critical minerals and economic security as key areas for cooperation. Both she and other European leaders have found a reliable ally in Carney as they deal with similar problems. In particular, they have faced Trump's aggressive use of tariffs and his threat to annex Greenland which is a sovereign territory of EU member Denmark. But "associate membership" of the EU does not currently exist and the process, if agreed, could take years. Earlier this year, Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz suggested - to a mixed reaction - that Ukraine could be granted this new status. cards.source_text: US House votes to hold billionaire Epstein associate Leon Black in contempt - Published The US House of Representatives has agreed to hold billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress for defying a legal summons related to its investigation into convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Black, who had business ties to Epstein, did not comply with a subpoena ordering him to appear before the House Oversight Committee earlier this month and share documents related to Epstein. Lawyers for Black, who has sued over the summons, called the contempt move "outrageous". After passage of the measure holding Black in contempt, Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer said: "No-one is above the law. We will continue to seek transparency for the American people and justice for survivors." In a statement shared with US media, lawyers for Black called the House move an "outrageous action that ignores the facts and the truth about Mr Black". "The full House is holding him in contempt without any regard to the active litigation challenging the lawfulness of the Committee's actions and the ethics complaint against Chairman Comer," they said. The measure, which passed by unanimous consent, means the matter will be referred to the US justice department, which will decide whether to criminally prosecute Black. In a written statement, the committee's top Democrat, congressman Robert Garcia, called the contempt vote "an important step towards justice and accountability". "We will continue to center the survivors in our fight to hold those responsible for these horrific crimes," he said. The private equity tycoon walked out of voluntary testimony before the House Oversight Committee in June after he was asked about nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) he may have signed, lawmakers said at the time. Black left Apollo Global Management, which he co-founded, amid scrutiny in 2021 over his Epstein ties. He has denied any wrongdoing with regards to his dealings with Epstein. The subpoenas, which ordered Black to share NDAs and give an on-camera deposition under oath, were issued after he left the committee meeting in June. Black has said he hired Epstein as a wealth management adviser, telling lawmakers in June that he gave Epstein $158m (£118m) for legitimate reasons. The billionaire has said he did not know about Epstein's crimes until he was charged with sex trafficking in July 2019. cards.source_text: US House holds billionaire Epstein associate Leon Black in contempt of Congress The US House of Representatives on Wednesday held billionaire investor Leon Black in contempt of Congress for defying two subpoenas in its investigation into sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The measure passed by unanimous consent and will be referred to the Justice Department, which will decide whether to pursue criminal charges. The US House of Representatives held billionaire investor Leon Black in contempt of Congress on Wednesday for defying subpoenas issued in its investigation into notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The resolution was adopted by unanimous consent, without a recorded vote, a day after the House Oversight Committee unanimously recommended the action. The matter will now be referred to the Justice Department, which will decide whether to pursue criminal charges. "No one is above the law. Leon Black defied two subpoenas, and the US House of Representatives acted swiftly to find him in contempt of Congress," panel chairman Jamie Comer said in a statement. "We will continue to seek transparency for the American people and justice for survivors in our investigation of the federal government's handling of the Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell criminal cases." Read moreSex trafficking in fashion: 'Outrageous that French legal system hasn't done anything by now' Black, the billionaire co-founder of Apollo Global Management, failed to appear for a September 3 deposition and did not fully comply with a separate subpoena seeking nondisclosure agreements. His lawyers called the House action "outrageous," accused lawmakers of rushing the process and said they would continue a court challenge to the subpoenas, US media reported. Black had appeared voluntarily before the committee in June, acknowledging that he paid Epstein $158 million for tax and estate-planning advice. But that session ended early after he declined to answer questions about some nondisclosure agreements, prompting lawmakers to demand further testimony and documents. Black has repeatedly denied wrongdoing and said he had no knowledge of Epstein's criminal activities. Epstein died in federal custody in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex-trafficking charges involving minors, in what authorities ruled a suicide. cards.source_text: UNITED NATIONS, September 17. /TASS/. Russia favors a comprehensive approach to Afghanistan, which envisages a trust-based dialogue with its authorities and is free from the language of pressure and blackmail, Russian Permanent Representative to the UN Vasily Nebenzya said. "Russia has consistently championed the development of a realistic comprehensive approach vis-a-vis Afghanistan," he told the UN Security Council meeting on Afghanistan. Such an approach is supposed to be grounded in objective analysis, a balanced assessment of the situation in the country, genuinely constructive engagement by the international community on the Afghan issue, full consideration of the needs of the Afghan people themselves, and a trust-based dialogue with the authorities covering all outstanding issues. This dialogue must be fully free from the language of pressure and blackmail." The Russian envoy went on to say that "such a comprehensive approach is shared by all regional actors barring none," particularly by the participants in the Moscow Format and its regional "Quartet." "We are heartened by the fact that the focus on pragmatic engagement with the Taliban also forms part of the "mosaic approach" articulated by UNAMA [the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan], including when it comes to securing diplomatic representation, lifting sanctions and unfreezing assets," Nebenzya continued. "Selective and biased approaches, as well as a fixation on human rights aspects - which is of particular interest to a certain group of Western donors - will lead nowhere."

cards.source_text: The discovery of the bodies of eight women around Johannesburg’s international airport, including five in the past week, has prompted an outpouring of fear, grief and anger over a lack of progress in tackling femicide. When Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo did not return after going for a run on 9 September, her eight-year-old daughter alerted relatives, who contacted police. The 38-year-old’s body was found on Saturday and identified by relatives on Monday. The news of her disappearance had gone viral. Police said in a statement on Saturday that four women’s bodies had been found since 15 July in Kempton Park, across the highway from OR Tambo international airport. All were half-naked and with visible bruising. On Monday and Tuesday, two more bodies were found in the town of Olifantsfontein about 15 miles north of Kempton Park. On Tuesday, police said another woman’s body had been found 25 miles to the south-east, naked and decomposed. The acting police minister, Firoz Cachalia, said on Wednesday that another woman’s body found in Olifantsfontein on 7 September, was being added to the investigation. “In this country we are prey,” Sakane Mokoena posted on Instagram after confirmation of the death of her friend and fellow runner Moselakgomo. South Africa has one of the highest rates of femicide in the world. Women were killed at a rate of 12.2 per 100,000 people in 2022, nearly six times the global rate, according to the UN Office on Drugs and Crime. For years, women have called on the South African government to take gender-based violence seriously. After hundreds of women protested on the eve of the G20 summit in Johannesburg in November 2025, President Cyril Ramaphosa declared it a national crisis. However, the lack of a concrete plan or action has frustrated campaigners – and women keep being killed. The latest deaths are being investigated by specialist officers, who said on Saturday: “Women in and around Kempton Park are urged not to walk or run alone, particularly in isolated areas. They should avoid secluded spaces, remain vigilant and, where possible, travel or exercise in groups.” South African women responded with anger at the idea that they had to be responsible for their own safety, with many runners noting they already took precautions, such as sharing routes. “We are tired of being told to be vigilant when women are already doing everything possible to stay alive,” said the advocacy group Women For Change. “It should not take a missing woman,

cards.title: 研究揭示英国金融体系深度嵌入奴隶贸易财富

entities.name: 英格兰银行（Bank of England）
entities.explain: 英国的中央银行，成立于1694年，1946年被政府国有化

entities.name: 跨大西洋奴隶贸易
entities.explain: 16至19世纪欧洲国家将数百万非洲人贩卖到美洲为奴的贸易体系

entities.name: 英国奴隶贩子登记册（Register of British Slave Traders）
entities.explain: 历史学家正在编纂的数据库，记录参与奴隶贸易的英国个人和机构

cards.summary: 历史学家编纂的《英国奴隶贩子登记册》研究发现，英格兰银行及整个英国金融体系与跨大西洋奴隶贸易的关联程度远超此前已知或承认的范围。英格兰银行创立时有数十名金融家同时是奴隶贸易的重要投资者。该研究揭示了奴隶贸易财富如何深深嵌入英国金融制度的根基。
cards.relevant: 这一研究推动英国社会重新审视其金融体系的历史原罪，对当前关于殖民赔偿和机构问责的讨论具有重要推动作用。
cards.context: 近年来，英国多所机构和大学陆续承认其历史财富与奴隶贸易的关联。此次研究首次系统性地揭示了英格兰银行这一核心金融机构与奴隶贸易的深度联系。
cards.source_analysis: 《卫报》报道，该报在殖民历史和奴隶贸易赔偿议题上通常持进步立场，倾向于支持对历史不公的揭露和问责。
cards.social_impact: 研究涉及英格兰银行创立时期的数十名董事和创始认购人，影响范围覆盖英国整个金融体系的历史叙事，可能推动赔偿讨论和机构道歉。
cards.source_text: The Bank of England and the British financial system were for centuries deeply involved in the enslavement and transatlantic trafficking of millions of African people, according to new research on Britain’s slavery history. Research by historians compiling the Register of British Slave Traders has found that the scale of the financial system’s involvement in enslavement is greater than previously known or acknowledged. The Bank of England, the central bank owned by the government since nationalisation by Clement Attlee’s Labour administration in 1946, had dozens of financiers involved in its foundation who were also significant investors in the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans. Dr Michael Bennett of the University of Sheffield, who has conducted extensive research on the Bank’s historical involvement in enslavement, has found that 24 directors were investors in the trafficking of enslaved African people. Four were among the London elites who were founding directors of the Bank in 1694. The other 20 were in office at Threadneedle Street over the next century. The last, Christopher Puller, was a shipper of weapons for the slave trade and co-owner of a 1786 voyage that trafficked enslaved people from the Gambia to Jamaica, according to the register. Puller was a director for 11 years before he died in 1789. Nine of the 24 were also governors of the Bank. Bennett also researched the founding subscribers to the Bank of England, finding that at least 30 invested in the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans. At their head were the king and queen of the day, William III and Mary II, who held shares in the Royal African Company. It is clear, Bennett said, that wealth generated from the slave trade formed part of the Bank’s initial capital. “Slave traders and their wealth were firmly embedded within Britain’s, especially London’s, private banks and financial corporations during the 17th and 18th centuries. They shaped the development of the financial system,” he said. “Banks and other institutions, like insurers, provided the financial services that supported, and made great wealth from, the transatlantic slave economy. “The Bank of England supported this system throughout, and directly provided financial services to the slave trade. Its clients included the Royal African Company and the South Sea Company.” An archetypal example of a Bank of England director in the register is John Rudge, the MP for Evesham. cards.summary: 美国宣布对部分南非人实施签证限制，理由是南非政府涉嫌对白人少数族群阿非利卡人进行种族歧视。特朗普在其第二任期内持续声称南非存在“白人种族灭绝”，并对南非的平权政策表示不满。此次公告未具体说明被限制入境的个人名单。
cards.relevant: 此举标志着特朗普政府将虚假的“白人种族灭绝”叙事转化为实际外交政策，可能进一步恶化美南关系。
cards.context: 特朗普自2025年上任以来多次声称南非白人遭受迫害，并于2025年2月宣布接受阿非利卡人作为难民。南非政府否认相关指控，称其平权政策旨在纠正种族隔离时代的不平等。
cards.source_analysis: 《卫报》报道，该报对特朗普政府的移民和种族政策持批评立场，报道中直接称特朗普的说法为“虚假”。
cards.social_impact: 签证限制影响部分南非公民的赴美权利，同时加剧了南非国内种族紧张关系，并使美南外交关系进一步复杂化。
cards.source_text: The US has announced visa restrictions on some South Africans as Donald Trump’s administration continues to claim that South Africa’s government racially discriminates against white minority Afrikaners. The announcement did not specify individuals who were barred from the US. Trump has spent his second term falsely claiming there is a “white genocide” in South Africa and railing against its affirmative action policies. Since the start of last year, the US has cut aid to South Africa, barred it from this year’s G20 summit in Miami and set up a refugee programme for Afrikaners and other South African racial minorities. Meanwhile, the Trump administration has been dismantling refugee and asylum programmes for people fleeing war and persecution. “The South African people are being failed by a government that is destroying its economy through an obsessive pursuit of racial grievance against the Afrikaner minority,” the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said in a post on X. “The South African government has consistently failed to adequately address rural crime, violent and dehumanising rhetoric, and race-based discriminatory policies against Afrikaners and other minority populations.” The US visa restrictions would target “foreign nationals who enact or enable policies that promote race-based discrimination, incite violence, or enable land confiscation without compensation in South Africa”, Rubio added. The US ambassador to South Africa, the conservative media activist Leo Brent Bozell III, said on X: “As has been made absolutely clear, the time for endless ‘dialogue’ has run its course … This visa restriction policy is only the first step in a series of escalatory measures that will show America’s firm resolve in this matter.” South Africa’s foreign ministry said in response that its policies were being misrepresented. “The announcement, once again, aligns with the mischaracterisation of South Africa’s domestic policies by fringe groups who wrongly portray themselves as representatives of “minorities” and Afrikaners in general,” the ministry spokesperson Chrispin Phiri said in a statement that was first published in Afrikaans.
